h1: The 6 Best 3D Printer Filaments Under $30 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Printer Filament Under $30: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 3D printer filaments under $30 scored on material, winding quality, strength and heat resistance across PLA, PETG and ABS.
summary: ELEGOO PLA is the filament to start with: 1 kg of 1.75 mm black PLA that is wound neatly and built to resist tangling. For parts that live in a warm car or near a heater, Polymaker ABS brings heat resistance and a low-odor formula. SUNLU PETG and Creality PETG cover tougher, weather-exposed prints. ELEGOO ABS is the cheaper heat-resistant alternative, and Creality PLA is the bulk-friendly bundle.
intro: Most filament failures blamed on a printer are really spool problems. A badly wound spool crosses over itself, snags at the extruder, and quietly ruins a 14-hour print at hour 13. Under $30 you can buy decent material, but the differences between listings lie in winding, consistency and what the polymer is built to survive, not the color of the box.

We reviewed six spools, all under $25 and all in 1.75 mm: two PLA, two PETG and two ABS. Each was ranked on the Primea framework, with the heaviest weight on material fit for typical hobby prints, how tangle-free and consistent the spool is described to be, and strength or heat resistance relative to the price. Your printer's enclosure and bed decide which polymer is realistic.

methodology.title: Material fit
methodology.description: PLA, PETG and ABS suit different parts, so each spool was judged against the jobs its polymer is built for.

methodology.title: Winding and tangle resistance
methodology.description: We rewarded spools described as neatly wound and less tangle-prone, since winding quality is the leading cause of failed long prints.

methodology.title: Strength and heat
methodology.description: Impact resistance, layer adhesion and heat resistance were compared against what each listing actually claims.

methodology.title: Printing experience
methodology.description: Odor, accuracy and how forgiving the material is to print were weighed, with low-odor ABS and easy PLA scoring well.

methodology.title: Value within the field
methodology.description: Every pick is under $25, so value was judged on what the spool gives you for that spend relative to the others in this guide.

whatMatters.factor: Pick the polymer for the part
whatMatters.detail: PLA prints easily and suits models, prototypes and desk gear. PETG is tougher and handles moisture and weather better. ABS survives heat and impact but is the hardest to print. Decide where the part will live, then choose the polymer. The wrong material will fail in use even when it prints perfectly.

A spool that crosses strands stalls the extruder mid-print. Listings that stress neat winding and low tangle, as the ELEGOO PLA does, point to better quality control. Look for those words on the listing, and check that the spool arrives sealed or vacuum packed so moisture has not already crept in.

Almost every consumer printer uses 1.75 mm filament, and the 1 kg spool is the standard unit for pricing. Check that the listing states both. A 2.85 mm spool will not feed a standard extruder at all, and a smaller spool may look cheap per box but costs more per kilogram.

ABS releases fumes while printing and warps if cooled too fast. Polymaker markets a low-odor formula, which helps, but both ABS spools here still call for a ventilated space and ideally an enclosure. If your printer is open and in a bedroom, choose PLA or PETG instead.

Filament absorbs water from the air, which causes popping, stringing and weak layers. PETG is especially sensitive. After opening a spool, store it in a sealed bag or box with desiccant. A spool that prints fine on day one and badly on day thirty is usually wet, not defective.

cards.label: PLA
cards.text: Easiest to print and fine for most hobby work. It softens in a hot car, so avoid it for parts that see heat. Picks: ELEGOO PLA, Creality PLA.

cards.label: PETG or ABS
cards.text: PETG gives toughness and weather resistance. ABS gives heat resistance but needs ventilation. Picks: SUNLU PETG, Creality PETG, Polymaker ABS, ELEGOO ABS.

howToChoose.note: Default to PLA unless the part needs heat, flex or outdoor survival.

rows: ELEGOO ABS 3D Printer Filament 1.75mm Black 1KG Strong Layer Adhesion

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Strong layer adhesion, heat or impact resistance stated on the listing, and a polymer matched to where the part will sit.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: Polymaker ABS for heat and mechanical use, SUNLU PETG for tough weather-exposed parts, and ELEGOO ABS for cheap heat-resistant parts.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You print for clients or run long jobs. Polymaker ABS and ELEGOO PLA are the safest picks here, because wasted prints cost more than a few dollars per spool.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You are just practicing or printing throwaway prototypes. Creality PLA and Creality PETG keep the spend low.

products.name: ELEGOO PLA 3D Printer Filament 1.75mm Black 1KG
products.verdict: Neatly wound, less-tangle PLA that is accurate and consistent for under $25.
products.description:
This is 1.75 mm black PLA on a 1 kg spool, described as accurate, consistent, less tangle-prone and neatly wound. It sits under $25, which makes it the sensible default spool for any hobby printer.

It wins because PLA is the polymer most prints should use, and the winding claims address the most common cause of failed jobs. Against the Creality PLA, which is sold as a bundle, the ELEGOO is the one aimed at consistent quality rather than volume. Against the PETG and ABS spools below, it gives up toughness and heat resistance in exchange for being the easiest to print.

Buy it for prototypes, desk accessories and models. The caveat is polymer: PLA softens in heat, so keep it away from parts that will sit in a warm car.
products.skipIf: Your part will face heat, weather or heavy impact.

products.name: Polymaker ABS Filament Black 1KG 1.75mm
products.verdict: A strong, heat-resistant ABS in a low-odor formula, built for functional parts.
products.description:
Polymaker's ABS is a 1 kg, 1.75 mm black spool marketed as strong and heat resistant, made for functional and mechanical parts. The formula is low odor, which matters for ABS, a polymer known for unpleasant fumes.

It takes second because heat resistance is the capability PLA cannot offer. Compared with the ELEGOO ABS, Polymaker's low-odor formula is the differentiator, and it makes a ventilated workshop feel less punishing. The tradeoff against the PLA picks is difficulty: ABS prints best in an enclosed machine.

Buy it for brackets, enclosures and parts near hot hardware. The caveat is that low odor is not no odor, so keep ventilation on and avoid printing it in a bedroom.
products.skipIf: You have an open-frame printer in a living space.

products.name: SUNLU PETG Filament 1.75mm
products.verdict: PETG with strong layer adhesion and the toughness the material is known for.
products.description:
SUNLU's PETG is a 1.75 mm filament marketed for excellent layer adhesion and enhanced toughness, with the toughness PETG is known for. It sits under $25.

It ranks third because PETG is the practical middle ground between PLA and ABS. It is tougher than PLA and far easier to print than ABS, so it suits parts that need some flex or outdoor survival. Against the Creality PETG, the SUNLU pitch is mechanical strength, while the Creality leans toward appearance with its transparent, glossy finish.

Buy it for functional prints, garden gear and parts that will see moisture. The caveat is that the listing text is thin on details like spool weight, so check that before assuming 1 kg.
cons: Prone to moisture if stored badly
products.idealFor: Functional parts that need toughness without ABS hassle.
products.skipIf: You want the easiest possible printing.

products.name: Creality PETG Filament 1.75mm
products.verdict: Glossy, transparent-capable PETG with a non-toxic material claim.
products.description:
Creality's PETG is a 1.75 mm filament pitched at high performance and strength, with a transparent, glossy finish and a non-toxic material claim. It is another under-$25 pick.

It lands fourth because the SUNLU PETG makes a stronger case on toughness and layer bonding, while this spool leads with looks. For lamp shades, display parts and anything where finish matters, the Creality is the more interesting choice. It is also a natural pairing if you already own a Creality printer.

Buy it for glossy or see-through prints. The caveat is that the listing leaves out temperature and spool weight details, so treat the first print as a calibration exercise.
products.skipIf: You want to compare the strongest PETG on paper.

products.name: ELEGOO ABS 3D Printer Filament 1.75mm Black 1KG Strong Layer Adhesion
products.verdict: Impact-resistant ABS with strong layer adhesion and a less-tangle winding.
products.description:
ELEGOO's ABS is a 1 kg, 1.75 mm black spool marketed for impact resistance, strong layer adhesion, and superior heat and water resistance. It is described as less-tangle and consistent.

It ranks fifth because the Polymaker ABS adds a low-odor formula, which is the more valuable feature in a home workshop. The ELEGOO wins by pairing ABS with the same winding story as its PLA, plus a clear layer-adhesion claim. For anyone already buying ELEGOO PLA, it is an easy step up.

Buy it if you need heat-resistant parts and want to stay under $25. The caveat is that, like all ABS, it needs ventilation, and the listing does not say that it is low odor.

products.name: Creality PLA 3D Printer Filament
products.verdict: A cost-effective PLA bundle for printers that burn through plastic.
products.description:
Creality's PLA is sold as a cost-effective filament bundle that is described as smooth, stable to print and durable. It falls under $25.

It ranks last because the listing gives the least specific information on this page, with no diameter, weight or winding claims. Against the ELEGOO PLA, which states 1.75 mm and 1 kg and the tangle-resistant winding, this one is vaguer. Its value comes from the bundle format, which can lower the cost per spool for frequent printers.

Buy it if you print often and want volume. The caveat is the vagueness, so confirm diameter and spool count on the listing before ordering.
products.idealFor: Frequent printers who want bulk plastic.
products.skipIf: You need clear diameter and spool details.

faq.q: Will these spools work on any 3D printer?
faq.a: Most consumer printers use 1.75 mm filament, and the ELEGOO and Polymaker spools state it. Check your printer's nozzle and hotend limits too, because ABS and some PETG need higher temperatures than a basic hotend allows.

faq.q: What is the biggest filament buying mistake?
faq.a: Choosing ABS because it sounds stronger, then printing it on an open printer. It warps and fumes. For most hobby parts the SUNLU PETG or ELEGOO PLA does the job with far less trouble.

faq.q: Is Polymaker ABS worth it over ELEGOO ABS?
faq.a: Polymaker's low-odor formula is the draw, and it makes sense in a shared workspace. ELEGOO ABS costs about the same bracket and stresses layer adhesion, so choose it only if the odor claim does not matter to you.

faq.q: How do I start printing with PETG?
faq.a: Load the SUNLU PETG or Creality PETG with a clean, well-leveled bed and print a small test piece first. PETG strings easily, so expect to tweak retraction and temperature before committing to a big model.

faq.q: How should I store opened spools?
faq.a: Seal each spool in a bag or box with desiccant packs as soon as you finish a print. PETG from SUNLU or Creality absorbs moisture fast, and wet filament causes stringing and weak layers.

faq.q: Can I mix PLA and ABS in one print?
faq.a: Not reliably. They need different temperatures and do not bond well, so stick to one polymer per part. If you need heat resistance and ease together, PETG such as the SUNLU spool is the usual compromise.

finalTake: ELEGOO PLA is the spool to buy first: neatly wound, consistent, and under $25. Need heat resistance? Polymaker ABS brings a low-odor formula, while ELEGOO ABS trims the cost further. For tough or weather-exposed parts, SUNLU PETG is the better material, and Creality PETG is the one to pick when finish matters. Creality PLA only makes sense as a bundle for heavy users.
